tasks.task: Write the visual spec for key screens

items.when: When wireframes are agreed and you need the steps from visual design to handoff in order
When each screen needs reading order, spacing, type style and colour role for every element
Before you settle a screen layout, to get three hand-made alternatives to the stock look
When the product has its own components and tokens and the screen must be built from them
When a new screen is drafted, to get a ready, fix-first or rethink call and a fix list
Before sign-off, to check hierarchy, alignment, spacing and states on each screen

tasks.task: Set type, spacing, grid and colour foundations

items.when: When a product has no agreed type scale, spacing scale, grid or colour roles
When brand colours and fonts are known and developers need them as named tokens
When AI or a new developer will build screens and needs one rules file to follow
When you start from a brief and want rules, checked colours, tokens and a spec in one run
When spacing is set by eye on each screen and nothing lines up across the product
Before the foundations are approved, to test each colour pair in light and dark

tasks.task: Explore clearly different visual directions for a product

items.when: When the client cannot describe the look, to pin down tone and feel in four answers
When the client shares products they like, to turn them into colour, type and feel
When one direction should be a tidy card grid, with tokens and states
When one direction should be calm and document-like, with warm greys and crisp borders
When one direction should be raw and blunt, to contrast with the safe options
When a direction is built, to score how generic it looks and what to change

tasks.task: Build a type scale from brand fonts

items.when: When brand fonts exist but text sizes differ from screen to screen
When there are no brand fonts, to compare pairs with sizes and line spacing for screens
When the client wants a quick shortlist of three font pairs to choose from
When the scale has many sizes and you cannot say what job each one does
When a text-heavy screen is set, to check size, spacing and line length where it is read

tasks.task: Set colour roles for light and dark themes

items.when: When the brand has one colour or none, to get a small palette with one job per colour
When you need each colour role in hex for light and dark, from surface to danger
When charts and data colours must work in dark mode too
Before approval, to measure every text and interface pair in both themes

tasks.task: Check contrast and dark mode across a product

items.when: When a scan or user flags low contrast, to list each pair, its ratio and the fix
When you have the colour tokens, to get the closest passing colour for each failing pair
When the check should go past colour to labels, focus order and other access problems
When there is no design file and the colours must be read from the live product

tasks.task: Write a component style sheet

items.when: When buttons, inputs, cards and other parts need sizes, colours and radius set once
When a part has only its default look and needs hover, focus, disabled and error
When one component needs variants, states, accessible behaviour and tokens in a brief
When components exist in code, to find hardcoded values and naming problems

tasks.task: Design empty, loading, error and success states

items.when: When a screen has only its happy path, to cover empty, loading, error, offline and success
When the states exist but the words blame the user or say nothing useful
When a state needs its label, message and button worded, to compare short options
When an error state shows what went wrong but not how to recover
When a component has changed, to find the states and variants still missing

tasks.task: Review screens and write before-and-after notes

items.when: When screens work but look off, to write each issue as a before and after a developer can apply
When everything on a screen has the same weight, to fix spacing, colour, type and depth
When you have the code, to list spacing, type and layout slips with a fix for each
When the input is a mockup or Figma link and you want usability and consistency notes
Before a release, to list the visual gaps that should block it
When the screen passes every check but still feels careless

tasks.task: Run a polish pass on a live product

items.when: Before a launch, demo or funding round, when the product works but looks unfinished
When the product looks generic and needs fixing in place without a rewrite
When one detail matters most, to try several versions and keep the best
When the app is shipped and you need the order to fix fit, flow and clarity
After the pass, to check motion, feel and the small details that make it look finished

tasks.task: Pull the current styles out of a live product

items.when: When there is no design file, only screenshots of the live product
When the product is a public website and you want its colours, fonts and spacing as files
When you also need the reasons behind a site's colour, type and layout choices
When you can see the code, to find where the same style is written many ways

tasks.task: Hand a final screen to developers

items.when: When a screen design is final and a developer will build it
When the handoff must cover tokens, component props, breakpoints and edge cases
When several screens go to build and you need the approval points in order
Before sending, to find missing states and write a review request developers can act on
After the build, to check the live screen against the spec with screenshots

tasks.task: Design or adapt screens for iPhone and Android

items.when: When a web or one-platform design must feel native on iPhone or Android
When you design a phone screen and need thumb reach and offline states covered
When you want native-feeling iPhone screens to compare on small and large sizes
When the screen is for iOS or Mac, to check it against Apple's current design rules
When the adapted screen needs its own spacing, type and states written for that platform

tasks.task: Design the look of a landing or marketing page

items.when: When the copy is ready, to get three on-brand page designs and a build brief
When the page must turn visitors into buyers and needs strict design rules
When you want a built page with a chosen look, checked in a browser
When the page is drafted, to check contrast, spacing, hierarchy and mobile
When the page is built, to write the remaining visual fixes as before and after

tasks.task: Design a dashboard or data-heavy screen

items.when: Before layout, to agree who reads the dashboard and which numbers they act on
When the layout is agreed and each tile, table and filter needs its type and spacing
When the dashboard is a wall of equal cards, to get three other arrangements
When charts need palettes that match the app and still read in dark mode
When decoration crowds out the numbers people need to compare
When a chart is drafted, to check the chart type and axes do not mislead

tasks.task: Design a form or multi-step flow screen

items.when: When a form needs its fields, error messages and a plan to raise completions
When a long form may work better in stages, to compare a stepped version
When inputs, selects and checkboxes need focus, filled, error and disabled looks
When the form is built, to check labels, focus order and error announcements

tasks.task: Specify motion and small interactions

items.when: When a screen needs its small moments planned: trigger, rule, feedback and loop
When a static design should be seen moving before anyone builds it
When motion is built, to judge whether it feels right or just busy
When a code change adds motion, to get a table of fixes and an approve or block call

tasks.task: Plan an icon set and favicon

items.when: When the product needs a small icon set and each icon must be tested for meaning
When you need vector drafts of icons in one style to compare and refine
When the logo must become a full favicon set with the link tags
Before shipping icons, to check each one reaches 3:1 against its background in both themes

tasks.task: Build a coded prototype of a screen

items.when: When you have a mockup or screenshot and want matching UI built from your own parts
When there is no mockup and you want a built page with careful colour, layout and motion
When a design question is open and a quick prototype would settle it
When you want a live preview of a screen idea in minutes to react to
When the team works in Figma and wants a clickable prototype from a prompt
When the prototype is built, to check it in a real browser at phone and desktop width

tasks.task: Audit a growing product for style drift

items.when: Each month, to find where the code has drifted from the design rules
When components multiply, to find hardcoded values and undocumented variants
When drift shows on screen, to write each fix as a before and after note
When old styles must be replaced, to list the changes and stage the move

tasks.task: Check screens still work after translation

items.when: When strings are translated, to check meaning and list where the layout may break
When longer words wrap or cut off, to write the spacing and size fixes

always.when: Before any work that must match the client's live site: colours, fonts and voice
Before a spec goes to developers, to catch typos and a part named two ways

helpers.when: When the flow, screen list or wording is not agreed and visuals would be guesswork
When the job is a full token set and component library, not a few screens
When the spec must become working code or the build needs fixing to match
When the product needs a full audit with keyboard and screen reader tests
When there is no logo, palette or brand font to build the interface on
When native platform parts or app store rules decide what the screen can do

gaps: No library item checks a screen against Android's Material Design rules; only Apple's rules are covered
No library item designs data tables and dense lists: column order, sorting, filters, density and row states
No library item shows three screen directions as pictures side by side; the style guides give words and code only
No library item covers Figma itself: variables, auto layout, component properties or file set-up
No library item measures spacing and alignment from a screenshot or compares a build with its design pixel by pixel
No library item designs an app icon or app store screenshots
No library item sets an illustration or image style for an interface
No library item plans breakpoints and how each screen reflows from phone to desktop
